cards.text: We're in Zechariah the prophet (Zechariah 1:1), and here comes the burden of the word of the LORD concerning Israel. The LORD introduces Himself as the One who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth and forms the spirit of man within him. Me? I introduce myself as "the guy with the mustache."
Now the LORD turns to Jerusalem and all the peoples around her. And He's about to make those nations STAGGER.

cards.question: The peoples around Jerusalem are about to stagger. What does the LORD make Jerusalem for them?
When the siege comes, only Jerusalem is surrounded and Judah is left alone.

cards.text: On that day, all the nations of the earth gather against Jerusalem, and the LORD makes her a heavy stone for all the peoples. It's like when your friend swears his dresser is "light" and you actually believe him.

cards.question: Jerusalem is a heavy stone for all the peoples. What happens to everyone who tries to heave it away?

answers.text: They will break it in pieces

cards.text: On that day, the LORD strikes every horse with panic and every rider with madness. I know that look, friend: that was ME the first time my mixer jumped to high speed.

cards.question: The LORD strikes the horses of the nations with blindness. But what does He do for the house of Judah?

answers.text: He keeps a watchful eye on them
He hides them in the hills
He leaves them to fight alone

cards.text: Watching all this, the leaders of Judah say something in their hearts. They say the people of Jerusalem are their strength.

cards.question: The leaders of Judah say the people of Jerusalem are their strength. Why?

answers.text: Because the LORD of Hosts is their God
Because Jerusalem has the strongest walls
Because the nations have all gone home

cards.text: Then the LORD makes the clans of Judah like a firepot in a woodpile, like a flaming torch among the sheaves. Friend, I once let parchment paper slide too close to my oven, so I know EXACTLY how this goes.

cards.question: The clans of Judah are like a firepot in a woodpile. What happens to the peoples around them?

answers.text: They are consumed on the right and the left
They put out the fire of Judah
They run to Judah for shelter

cards.question: While the fire of Judah spreads among the peoples, the people of Jerusalem remain secure.

cards.text: Now, who does the LORD save first? You'd think the big city, or the house of David, the royal family of King David, goes straight to the front of the line.

cards.question: Out of everyone in Judah and Jerusalem, who does the LORD save first?
The LORD saves the tents of Judah first, so the glory of the house of David and the people of Jerusalem won't be ___ than the glory of Judah.
On that day, the LORD defends the people of Jerusalem. Even the weakest among them will be like whom?

cards.text: The WEAKEST one, friend! In my bakery that's me after carrying one tray of cookies, and even I would be like DAVID. And the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them.

cards.question: So on that day, the LORD sets out to ___ all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

cards.text: Right after all that fighting, the LORD says He will pour something out on the house of David and the people of Jerusalem.

cards.question: What does the LORD pour out on the house of David and the people of Jerusalem?

answers.text: A spirit of grace and prayer

cards.text: And then the LORD says they "will look on Me, the One they have pierced." Read that line twice, friend.

cards.question: They look on the One they have pierced. How does the LORD describe the way they mourn for Him?

answers.text: Like someone mourning an only child
Like someone missing an old friend
Like someone losing a day's wages

cards.text: Hold on to that line. When a soldier pierces Jesus' side at the cross, John quotes this very Scripture (John 19:34-37).

On that day, the wailing in Jerusalem will be as great as the wailing of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo. The whole land mourns: the houses of David, Nathan and Levi, the clan of Shimei, all the remaining clans, and their wives.

cards.question: When the land mourns, all the clans gather into one big crowd to grieve together.

cards.text: Then, on that day, a fountain is opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem. After all those tears, friend, here comes the turn.

cards.question: The fountain is opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem to cleanse them from ___ and impurity.

cards.text: The LORD of Hosts says He will erase the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. Erased and forgotten: I know that feeling from my years in the junk drawer, except the idols actually EARNED it.

cards.question: Along with the idols, the LORD also removes the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.

cards.text: So what if somebody still prophesies after that? His own father and mother, the ones who bore him, step in.

cards.question: A man keeps prophesying after the LORD removes the prophets from the land. What do his father and mother say he has done?

answers.text: Spoken falsely in the name of the LORD
Turned away from working the land
Stolen from the house of the LORD

cards.text: They tell him he shall not remain alive, and when he prophesies, they pierce him through. On that day, every prophet who prophesies will be ashamed of his vision.

cards.question: An ashamed prophet stops putting on something he used to wear in order to deceive. What is it?

cards.text: Now listen to how this guy describes himself. Friend, that résumé just got a FULL rewrite.

cards.question: How does the ashamed prophet describe himself now?

answers.text: Not a prophet but a servant who works the land
Not a prophet but a priest in the temple
Not a prophet but a merchant from Tarshish

cards.question: Someone asks the ashamed prophet about the wounds on his chest. What does he say?

answers.text: He got them in the house of his friends
He got them fighting the nations
He got them from a wild animal

cards.text: Then the tone shifts hard. The LORD of Hosts calls a sword to awake against His Shepherd, against the man who is His Companion.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says to strike the Shepherd. What happens to the sheep?

answers.text: They will find a new shepherd

cards.text: And the LORD says He will turn His hand against the little ones. On the night Jesus is arrested, He quotes the line about the Shepherd and the scattered sheep, telling His disciples they will all fall away (Matthew 26:31, 47-50).

cards.question: In all the land, the LORD says two-thirds will be cut off and perish, but a ___ will be left in it.

cards.text: That third, the LORD will bring through the fire. Every batch I make goes into that oven raw and comes out READY, so trust me, I understand this picture.

cards.question: Why does the LORD bring that third through the fire?

answers.text: To refine them like silver and test them like gold
To burn them away from the land for good
To punish them and then leave them behind

cards.question: The LORD says that when the refined third call on His name, He will answer them.

cards.text: And then the best part, friend: the LORD will say, 'They are My people,' and they will say, 'The LORD is our God.' Out of the fire and right into the family.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. There are 7 multiple choice cards (3, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17) against 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "Watching all this" says the leaders of Judah speak because they see the LORD's acts. Zechariah 12:5 only says "Then." It never connects what they say to anything they watched.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup names the house of David and the city as what "you'd think" comes first. Those are two of the three answers on card 15, so the line points the baker straight to the third answer, the tents of Judah.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. There are 6 multiple choice cards (2, 4, 13, 15, 17, 18) against 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "Right after all that fighting" adds a timing the text doesn't give. Zechariah 12:10 only says "Then."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Nathan, Levi and Shimei appear here for the first time, and the card doesn't say who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Too many choice cards in this stop can only be answered by luck. Card 7 (each clan mourns on its own), card 11 (the prophets are removed too), card 15 (the hairy cloak) and card 18 (wounds from the house of his friends) all lack the context needed to reason them out. Card 18 also follows another choice card, and the wounds were never set up on any card.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The question already says two-thirds are cut off. That rules out "half" and "tenth" by simple math, so the right answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
